dialect.guess: GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) / ORCA JMA medical system dialect
evidence: LINKAGE SECTION with USING clause on PROCEDURE DIVISION
CALL 'ORCDBMAIN' USING pattern consistent with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL
COPY directives referencing .INC files typical of ORCA JMA system
grpsys continuation-line tag used as inline comment/label

purpose.summary: This subprogram is part of the ORCA JMA standard medical receipt software (Japan Medical Association). It reads reception (uketuke) records from a database table, searches for a matching record based on patient ID, department, and insurance combination, and updates the transmission flag (SRFLG) on the matching record to mark it as sent.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical billing (Japanese medical receipt system)

notable_features: Japanese EUC or Shift-JIS encoded comments (rendered as mojibake in latin-1 decoding)
Custom database access via CALL 'ORCDBMAIN' (DBSELECT, DBFETCH, DBUPDATE, DBCLOSECURSOR pattern)
COPY of multiple .INC and named copybooks (CPUKETUKE.INC, COMMON-SPA, CPORCSDAY.INC, CPORCSLNK.INC, MCPAREA, MCPDATA.INC)
grpsys tag used as inline source annotation/label on certain lines
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — database access abstracted through ORCDBMAIN
ACCEPT FROM DATE for system date retrieval
COMPUTE to convert 2-digit year to 4-digit year (Y2K-style handling)
verdict.notes: The file was decoded with latin-1 but contains Japanese text encoded in EUC-JP or Shift-JIS, causing mojibake in the comment lines. The 'grpsys' tokens appearing at the start of some lines are not standard COBOL — they appear to be a source-management annotation or conditional compilation tag specific to the ORCA system. The program has no COPY count recorded mechanically (copy_count=0) despite clearly containing COPY statements; this may be a mechanical indicator limitation. The program is part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system used in Japan.
